critical_findings.title: The inherited S35 worker rejects the V5 supervisor-watchdog-worker parent topology
critical_findings.finding: The unchanged S35 worker requires launch_ticket.parent_pid to equal os.getppid(). V5 bound_ticket requires the same field to equal the outer supervisor PID and returns the document unchanged. V5 then forks the worker from the watchdog, and the capability consumer independently confirms that os.getppid() is the watchdog PID. Therefore the exact production worker reaches mutually incompatible parent predicates before any scientific import.
critical_findings.independent_evidence: Both exact-hash static probes reproduced all sides of the contradiction: the legacy actual-PPID predicate remains, the ticket is supervisor-bound and unmodified, the watchdog owns the worker, and no derivation rewrite transfers the legacy predicate to the watchdog identity.
critical_findings.impact: A formally authorized V5 attempt cannot reach the full resource gate or generation. It would consume the unique execution lease and fail before scientific import, so V5 is not runnable as frozen.
critical_findings.required_fix: Define separate supervisor_pid and watchdog_pid identities, bind both only after the watchdog reports the owned worker, and make the inherited worker validate its actual direct parent without also requiring the same field to represent the supervisor. Freeze and review a new complete source set and add a synthetic test that executes the derived worker through this exact check with all later operations stubbed.

critical_findings.title: The watchdog can certify cleanup while a detached closed-output descendant remains alive
critical_findings.finding: Watchdog cleanup terminates and probes only the worker process group. A descendant that creates another session leaves that group. The author late-descendant self-test forks a child that stays inside the worker group, so it does not cover this case. The exact watchdog nevertheless reports cleanup_complete=true and sends a success acknowledgement while the detached descendant is alive.
critical_findings.independent_evidence: Under both isolated interpreters, a disposable descendant that detached from the worker group and closed standard input/output/error remained alive after WATCHDOG_RECEIPT claimed cleanup complete and the watchdog exited zero. The review harness then removed it and confirmed it was gone.
critical_findings.impact: Monitor loss or a terminal worker can leave untracked work running while the evidence chain says the attempt is clean. The outer seal treats the watchdog acknowledgement as sufficient, so the stated no-survivor boundary is not enforced.
critical_findings.required_fix: Use an OS-enforced containment mechanism available on the target platform, or maintain a durable descendant identity ledger that remains authoritative across reparenting and process-group changes. The watchdog and outer success gate must require every registered descendant gone. Add pre-registration and late-registration tests in which a descendant changes session and closes all inherited output descriptors.

major_findings.title: A terminal write failure can leave a success-shaped supervisor seal
major_findings.finding: write_new_json_at creates, syncs and closes the requested JSON file before syncing its directory. If the final directory sync fails, the helper raises after the success-status file exists. The outer exception path sees the seal name occupied and does not publish a failure seal. The process returns failure, but the persistent supervisor_seal.json has the success status and a success-shaped body.
major_findings.independent_evidence: Both isolated interpreters reproduced this state using only a disposable directory and a synthetic sync fault; no formal path or candidate main was used.
major_findings.impact: The terminal directory contains contradictory evidence: a non-successful outer return and a success-shaped sole seal. A later status-only reader can misclassify the attempt, and the fixed path prevents a clean failure receipt at that name.
major_findings.required_fix: Publish a non-success provisional record first and make success depend on a separate create-only terminal commit whose completed write and directory sync are externally checked. Define an exact terminal directory shape that rejects an uncommitted success-shaped body and add deterministic post-file/pre-directory-sync failure tests.

major_findings.title: The final seal write is not followed by canonical execution-path identity validation
major_findings.finding: The last execution.validate() occurs before terminal receipts are read and before the supervisor seal is written. The seal is written through the held directory descriptor, then sealed=true is set and success may return without another path-to-descriptor identity check. If the canonical execution name changes during that gap, the success seal is written into the renamed held inode rather than the current canonical execution directory.
major_findings.independent_evidence: Both disposable interpreter probes confirmed that the exact held-directory writer returns a digest and writes only to the renamed original inode after the final validation point; a subsequent validate would reject, but the candidate success path has no such post-write validation.
major_findings.impact: A zero-returning invocation can lose the canonical path to its authoritative seal, contradicting the protocol's claim that execution identity is retained through terminal publication. This is a path-identity ambiguity even when the held inode itself remains intact.
major_findings.required_fix: Retain the seal file descriptor through publication, bind its inode, sync it and the directory, then revalidate the entire canonical ancestor and execution chain before deciding success. If revalidation fails, success must be impossible and a fixed held-parent failure record must be emitted.
